stats_by_spread.financing_note: S-21 (2026-09-11): every figure in this file is computed with ZERO cost of leverage, because LEAN charges none - DefaultBrokerageModel.GetMarginInterestRateModel returns MarginInterestRateModel.Null, whose ApplyMarginInterestRate is an empty method body, and InteractiveBrokersBrokerageModel does not override it. This book carries 1.50x gross against 1.00x of equity, i.e. a debit balance on 83.3% of sessions averaging 0.493x of equity, and it has never paid a cent of interest on it. Charged at IBKR Pro's published tiers on the historical effective fed funds rate (FRED DFF), the 0 bp column becomes 23.087% / 0.939 / DD 24.1% (run 20260911T194431Z, -1.316 CAR) and the 2 bp column becomes 21.745% / 0.882 / 25.4% (run 20260911T195453Z, -1.323). The correction is out-of-sample weighted more than two to one: IS 2012-2019 16.791% against 17.698% (-0.907), OOS 2020-2026 30.774% against 32.801% (-2.027), because the benchmark went from ~0.1% to 5% and 82% of the sample's total interest was incurred in 2023-2026. At today's 3.63% benchmark the forward-looking drag is about 2.0 CAR points a year, not 1.3. About half is the irreducible cost of money (benchmark-only: 0.56 of 1.11 simple points) and half is the broker's markup, which a larger account pays less of. THIS IS NOT A DEFECT AND NOT A PROMOTABLE COLUMN: it is a real cost the paper account has been paying since its first fill, there is nothing wrong with the runner, and the only thing it corrects is the expectation. S1_FINANCING defaults off so the whole ledger stays on one scale (S-17's precedent with S1_SLIPPAGE_BPS), and scripts/evaluate.py REFUSES any run recorded with S1_FINANCING=on as not comparable rather than judging it against these columns. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s21.py --probe --report.
stats_by_spread.deployed_expectation_note: S-22 (2026-09-11): the three instrument corrections charged TOGETHER. S-17 (no spread), S-19 (the runner's clock) and S-21 (no financing) each priced one defect alone; the full-period LEAN factorial charges them in every combination and they are INDEPENDENT - control 24.403 / spread 2bp 23.068 / financing 23.087 / clock bound lag1 21.384 / all three 18.785 against a multiplicative null of 18.811 (interaction -0.026 CAR points, every pair inside 0.021), pre-registered in scripts/_s22_runs.sh before any cell ran. So defects on this sleeve may be priced one at a time and composed afterwards. The headline number needs the harness LEAN cannot be, because the engine cannot fill at the close of the session it decided in: scripts/sweep_s19.py now takes an optional financing= argument (default None, every S-19 row bit-identical) and scripts/sweep_s22.py --book runs it. That book agrees with LEAN's financing drag at the backtest convention (-1.357 vs -1.316) and its fully-charged lag1 cell lands 0.03 CAR points from LEAN's own triple. On it, THE DEPLOYED 15:45 BOOK, CHARGED 2 BP OF SPREAD AND IBKR PRO FINANCING, EARNS 19.640% - 19.954% in LEAN units, -4.449 points against the 24.403% above - and 19.415% at today's 3.63% cost of money. Read every figure in this file against ~20%, not 24.4%: the headline is about 18% high. It is not a defect and nothing is broken; the paper account has been paying all three since its first fill. The correction is out-of-sample weighted more than two to one (IS 2012-2019 14.194% against 17.698%, OOS 2020-2026 24.259% against 32.801%) and it costs return rather than risk - drawdown across the whole factorial moves 23.700 -> 23.000 and realized vol 0.155 -> 0.156. The clock third of it is the one thing that is fixable, and BLOCKERS.md prices the pre-open task move at +1.85 CAR points on this honestly-costed book at today's rates (19.415 -> 21.264). Nothing was promoted or defaulted: S1_SLIPPAGE_BPS stays 0.0, S1_SIGNAL_LAG stays 0 and S1_FINANCING stays off. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s22.py --report --book.
stats_by_spread.auction_note: S-24 (2026-09-11): what the two price legs in this file actually are, measured against the official SIP auction prints for all nine sleeve names over 2016-2026 (2,683 sessions, scripts/sweep_s24.py --report). THE CLOSE IS EXACT: the implied close factor store_close/sip_close has a median day-over-day change of exactly 0.000 bps for every one of the nine, so the daily store's close IS the official closing cross to the cent on every session, and the deployed 15:45 convention has always been marked at the right price. THE OPEN IS NOT: Yahoo's daily open is the first consolidated print of the session, not the primary opening auction, and the implied open factor wobbles 0.6-1.5 bps a day for six of the nine (XLE misses by 8-11 bps on some sessions). This matters for LEAN too, because the engine fills MarketOnOpen orders at that same store open. It is a NOISY benchmark rather than a flattering one - the store's open sits a sleeve-weighted +0.050 bps from the cross with a median of exactly 0.000 and mixed signs - so the effect on any figure in this file is small, but it is not zero: re-filling the pre-open book at the real cross costs 0.149 CAR points, about 0.22 bps of one-way execution cost at S-17's 0.68 CAR points per bp. The practical consequence is for the pre-open MOO move in BLOCKERS.md, which is worth +1.98 CAR points at the real cross rather than +2.13 at the store's open, with a band to +3.20 because an MOO order is matched in a single-price call auction and crosses no quoted spread at all. Nothing in this file was recomputed and no number above moved. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s24.py --report --cross.
stats_by_spread.leg_note: S-25 (2026-09-12): WHICH HALF OF THE DAY EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS EARNED IN. The deployed book holds around the clock and is paid twice a session; scripts/sweep_s25.py splits its P&L at the open on 3,689 sessions (2012-2026) after reproducing scripts/sweep_s19.py's deployed cell to the digit (CAR 22.192150%, 5,052 orders, leg residual 5.33e-16 of equity, and the costed cell landing on S-22's independent 19.640%). THE SPLIT IS +8.103 BPS/DAY OVERNIGHT (t +6.80, 94% of the total) AGAINST +0.738 INTRADAY (t +0.47), with annualized leg volatility 0.115 and 0.151 against 0.188 total, correlation -0.014 - the leg that pays 94% of the return carries 61% of the risk. Quoted against an always-invested control scaled every day to this book's own 1.25x gross (the daily twin of F-5's always-long rule), THE SELECTION DIFFERENCE IS +3.087 BPS/DAY AT t +4.20 OVERNIGHT (SPY control +3.081, t +3.79) AND -0.314 AT t -0.37 INTRADAY, agreeing in both halves (+2.993 t +3.62 IS, +3.200 t +2.51 OOS): fourteen years find no intraday content in this ranking. Two artifacts were ruled out rather than assumed away - the ex-date credit inside the overnight leg is +0.683 bps/day for the book against +0.826 for the control, so price-only the excess is LARGER (+3.231, t +4.36), and on S-24's official opening crosses the leg reads +8.864 against the store's +8.887 over 2,683 sessions. NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTABLE AND NO NUMBER ABOVE MOVED: the two conditional books that trade one leg only are refused at a NEGATIVE breakeven (overnight-only 13.113% at 0 bp and -0.555% at 2 bp on 1,248x equity of annual turnover; intraday-only -3.032% and -18.269%; paired -7.785 and -15.395 bps/day at t -4.97 and -12.19), i.e. they lose before a cent of cost is charged. The consequence for future work on this sleeve is that a candidate spending turnover on what the book holds BETWEEN the open and the close is spending it where the evidence is zero, and the consequence for BLOCKERS.md is that the pre-open MOO move's whole payoff is intraday (+0.604 bps/day, t +1.43; overnight -0.006) while the in-place alternative is worth +0.18 CAR points. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s25.py --dividends --preopen --cross.
stats_by_spread.hedge_note: S-26 (2026-09-12): WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO ACT ON THE LEG SPLIT ABOVE, AND WHY IT IS REFUSED. S-25 showed all of this book's measurable alpha is overnight and none of it is intraday, and that the leg cannot be isolated by trading the equity book (1,248x turnover, negative at zero cost). The only remaining route is a futures overlay: short h x beta x equity of the index from the open to the close on a causal trailing beta. scripts/sweep_s26.py prices it on the same harness (identity: hedge=None, scale=1.0 reproduces 22.192150% / 5,052 orders, residual 5.33e-16; the costed cell lands on 19.640% again), with two default-inert arguments added to sweep_s25.legs_simulate. THE PROXY IS VALIDATED, NOT ASSUMED: over F-2a's 313 ES cash sessions corr(ES, SPY open->close) = 0.9994, slope 0.9984, basis sd 2.1 bps/session, so no CME history is needed to price an index overlay. Charged 2 bp of equity spread, IBKR Pro financing and F-2a's 0.488 bps futures round trip, the grid reads 19.640% / 1.047 / DD 24.04 unhedged then 18.972 / 18.174 / 17.263 / 16.224 at h = 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00, with Sharpe peaking at a HALF hedge (1.124) and drawdown falling to 20.77: the overlay converts return into risk reduction, roughly fairly. VOL-MATCHED TO THIS BOOK'S OWN 0.1883 ON THE REAL MACHINERY, h=0.50 EARNS 20.837% / SHARPE 1.100 (+1.197 CAR POINTS), WINS BOTH HALVES (IS 15.041 vs 14.317, OOS 27.627 vs 25.967) AND STAYS INSIDE REG-T AT 1.83x MAX GROSS - AND IT IS REFUSED BECAUSE ITS DRAWDOWN IS 26.02 AGAINST 24.04, 1.99 POINTS WORSE AGAINST THE 1.0-POINT TOLERANCE IN 'criteria' ABOVE. h=1.00 is refused on CAR full period and in both halves. Nothing reaches |t| = 2 (paired +0.395 at t +0.60). The breakeven is the durable number: +1.108 bps a round trip at h=0.50 and +0.316 at h=1.00 against ES's 0.488 (full tick 0.856, MES 0.744), so THE HALF HEDGE CLEARS THE CHEAPEST INSTRUMENT ON FILE BY 2.3x AND DIES ON RISK RATHER THAN ON COST - the first candidate in this repository to do so. The placebo is what makes the split actionable knowledge rather than an artifact: the identical overlay on the OVERNIGHT leg costs -4.310 bps/day at t -4.14 (7.598% / DD 28.60) against the intraday overlay's -1.373 at t -1.02, the only |t| > 2 in the file. NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTABLE, NO NUMBER ABOVE MOVED, AND NOTHING COULD SHIP IN ANY CASE: an overlay needs the owner's consent to hold futures, and the h=1.00 hedge is below one ES contract on 65.4% of sessions on this book's equity path. The un-relevered h=0.50 book (18.174% / 1.124 / DD 22.45) is a priced risk-posture option in BLOCKERS.md, not a candidate. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s26.py (--stage a / b / c).
stats_by_spread.rank_note: S-27 (2026-09-12): HOW TO READ leg_note AND hedge_note ABOVE - the split is an ATTRIBUTION, NOT A SIGNAL RECIPE. The obvious inference from S-25 is that a ranking built on the leg the book is paid in should rank better, so scripts/sweep_s27.py built three synthetic price indices per ticker from the same adjusted store (cc = the close series, on = compounded close[d-1]->open[d], id = compounded open[d]->close[d], leg identity (1+on)(1+id)=(1+cc) exact to 2.22e-16), recomputed the champion's own 20/60/120/252 blend on each, and ranked the shipped algorithm on it through F-3's S1_ML_SCORES hook in ML_MODE='rank'. No runner-loaded file was modified and the identity cell reproduces the deployed book to the digit (22.192150%, 5,052 orders). THE INFERENCE IS WRONG. The close-to-close score and the overnight-only score have THE SAME RANK IC on the next session's overnight leg (+0.0574 at t +7.25 and t +7.32 over 3,689 sessions), but the quantity this book collects - the top-3-minus-equal-weight spread at top_n=3 - is +2.106 bps/day (t +3.24) for the shipped score against +1.311 (t +2.04) for the overnight one, and the gap holds in both halves (IS 2.176 vs 0.947, OOS 2.021 vs 1.740). Nothing forecasts the intraday leg: the best cell in that column is the shipped score at +0.0141 (t +1.81) with a NEGATIVE spread of -0.727. As books, charged 2 bp and IBKR Pro financing on the deployed convention, overnight-ranked earns 11.751% / Sharpe 0.656 / DD 35.210 and intraday-ranked 13.167% / 0.778 / 27.591 against the deployed 19.640% / 1.047 / 24.037 - paired -2.619 bps/day (t -2.41) and -2.270 (t -2.08), worse in both halves, and the primary breaches the 35% absolute drawdown limit in 'criteria' below. It is not an exposure artifact: mean gross is 1.24x against 1.25x and the same-gross always-invested overnight excess is +3.087 bps/day (t +4.20) for the shipped ranking against +1.686 (t +1.86) overnight-ranked and +1.183 (t +1.51) intraday-ranked, on LOWER turnover (131x equity/yr vs 240x). So the leg that pays is better forecast by the whole trend than by its own history, and no number above moves. One by-product, post hoc and sign-stable in both halves: the overnight score forecasts the next INTRADAY leg negatively, top-3-minus-EW -2.230 bps/day at t -3.30 (IS -2.182, OOS -2.290) - recorded, not pursued, and on names AGENTS.md's disjointness rule bars the intraday sleeve from. S1_ML_SCORES stays unset in every deployed path. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s27.py --stage ab.
stats_by_spread.risk_note: S-28 (2026-09-12): WHAT THE THREE NOTES ABOVE IMPLY FOR THE SIZING MACHINERY, AND THE ONE PLACE THE LEG SPLIT CHANGES THIS BOOK. Every figure in this file is produced by a book sized as target_vol / sigma with sigma measured CLOSE TO CLOSE, on a quantity 61% of whose variance is the intraday leg that leg_note showed pays nothing. scripts/sweep_s28.py replaces that estimator and only that estimator, through a new default-inert hook in the shipped signals.py (S1_VOL_RETURNS / set_vol_returns, F-3's S1_ML_SCORES pattern; the I-1 gate was re-run after the edit, 3,689/3,689 dates, 5,021 orders both sides, PASS). The identity cell reproduces the deployed book to the digit (22.192150%, 5,052 orders) and the leg identity holds to 2.220e-16. THE PREMISE IS NOT EMPTY: pooled over the nine names on 59,662 observations, every leg forecasts its own next-21-session realized vol better than the pooled estimate does (cc->cc 0.7260, on->on 0.6764 against cc->on 0.6608, id->id 0.7492), though the two estimators are 0.9029 correlated in log level with sigma_on/sigma_cc = 0.5888. ALL FOUR BOOKS ARE REFUSED, charged 2 bp and IBKR Pro financing on the deployed convention. The RAW legs are a leverage change and nothing else - overnight vol is 0.59x close-to-close vol, so the scale sits at its cap on 86.3% of sessions and the book earns 20.333% for a 32.031% drawdown (intraday-raw 20.084 / 30.196) by deleting the crisis de-risking S-16 and O-1b already priced. The LEVEL-MATCHED primary, rescaled by a causal expanding-window factor, earns 19.400% / Sharpe 1.049 / DD 21.622 against the deployed 19.640% / 1.047 / 24.037 - refused on CAR, paired -0.100 bps/day at t -0.92. THE PLACEBO IS WHAT MAKES IT READABLE: the identical construction on the leg this book is NOT paid in moves it the opposite way (id_k +0.16 CAR for +1.43 points of drawdown against on_k's -0.24 CAR for -2.42), same machinery and same turnover to 4%. POST HOC AND LABELLED AS SUCH, at matched risk (scale 1.015 on S-26's argument, realized vol 0.1883 both sides): 19.613% / 1.046 / DD 21.931, i.e. A DEAD HEAT IN RETURN (paired -0.009 bps/day, t -0.08) FOR 2.1 POINTS LESS DRAWDOWN, refused by 0.027 CAR points, passing OOS 2020-2026 on every criterion (26.007 vs 25.967, DD 20.67 vs 24.04) and failing IS 2012-2019 (14.254 vs 14.317, DD 21.72 vs 20.94). Read it with its sample: the vol target, rather than the 0.75 margin budget, sizes this book on only 2.8% of sessions (4.7% under on_k), nothing here reaches |t| = 2, and the whole difference is 3.8 points off the 2022 drawdown against 0.7 points added to the 2015-16 one. NOTHING IS PROMOTABLE AND NO NUMBER ABOVE MOVED: S1_VOL_RETURNS is unset in every deployed path and the shipped estimate is the close-to-close pct_change it has always been. The matched-risk column is filed in BLOCKERS.md as a priced risk-posture option beside S-26's half hedge - the cheaper of the two, because it needs no futures permission and no Reg-T decision - and it is the owner's call rather than the loop's only because 'criteria' below is return-first. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s28.py.
stats_by_spread.regime_note: S-29 (2026-09-12): WHAT THE CRISIS SWITCH IN THIS BOOK IS, AND WHY A BETTER VOLATILITY FORECAST MAKES IT WORSE. Volatility decides this book twice: the vol target decides SIZE (S-28 measured it binds on 2.8% of sessions) and `risk_on` decides DIRECTION - it holds nothing at all whenever SPY's trailing 20-session REALIZED volatility exceeds 1.5x its own one-year median, which is 590 of the 3,689 sessions behind every figure in this file. scripts/sweep_s29.py swaps that input for the market's forward-looking one through a third default-inert hook in the shipped signals.py (S1_REGIME_SERIES / set_regime_series, F-3's pattern; the gate is scale-free, so no constant is re-tuned), with BOTH deploy gates re-run after the edit - compare_orders.py 3,689/3,689 at 5,021 orders and a full LEAN control reproducing OrderListHash a6d6224ce9c70091e5bfa8e96f046bf3 (5,128 orders / 24.403% / 0.994 / 23.700% / $27,199.76, run 20260912T093609Z) - and two identities to the digit (the shipped level through the hook gives 22.192150% / 5,052 orders, and a standalone gate series reproduces the book's own risk-off days 3,689/3,689). THE PREMISE IS NOT EMPTY, IT IS EMPHATIC: against the realized volatility of the NEXT 21 sessions, log-log correlation is 0.4985 for the shipped estimate, 0.6361 for VIX, 0.5326 for a VIX made five sessions stale and 0.6857 for SPY's own 1-month ATM implied vol (Theta, 2017-2026), on identical samples - the market's forecast is a quarter better than the book's own. AND THE BETTER FORECAST IS THE WORSE SWITCH. Measured on an UNGATED version of this book (threshold 99, the only non-circular reference, since the deployed book is flat on its own off days by construction), every session earns +10.01 bps/day, the sessions the realized gate removes earn +8.72, the sessions VIX removes earn +20.07, and the 60 sessions VIX removes that realized does not earn +36.56 at t +2.01 - the only |t| > 2 in the diagnostic. Charged 2 bp of spread and IBKR Pro financing on the deployed convention, the primary VIX gate at the shipped threshold earns 15.901% / Sharpe 0.842 / DD 37.758 against the deployed 19.640% / 1.047 / 24.037, failing every criterion in the full period and in BOTH halves (IS 13.251 vs 14.317, OOS 18.763 vs 25.967) and breaching the 35% absolute limit; the PRE-REGISTERED off-rate-matched column, whose threshold (1.2688) was solved on the in-sample half alone so the gate steps aside on the same 14.3% of sessions and the 'it is only more exposure' explanation is removed, is the WORST book on the page at 12.188% / 0.729 / 31.540, PAIRED -2.612 BPS/DAY AT t -3.06 - so the loss is in the TIMING, not the exposure. The placebo triggers the pre-registered withdrawal condition anyway: making VIX five sessions STALE, deliberately destroying a third of its forecast advantage, makes the book BETTER (16.666% full period and 15.911% in-sample against 15.901 and 13.251), so nothing here is paying for forecast quality. It is not a tuning question - across thresholds 1.25/1.40/1.50/1.60/1.75/2.00 the VIX gate loses to the realized gate at every one of the six and draws down 33-41% at every one - and it is not a VIX-construction artifact, because the independent SPY ATM implied series (the BEST forecaster in the table) agrees in sign on its own 2018-2026 window at 15.926% / 0.791 / DD 35.193 against the shipped 21.219% / 1.036 / 24.040. TWO THINGS IT SETTLES IN PASSING, and they are about the numbers above rather than about the candidate. (1) The shipped 1.50 threshold is a SHELF, NOT A SPIKE: it is the Sharpe maximum of the realized row (1.047 against 0.996 / 1.001 / 1.011 / 0.988 / 0.999) with both neighbours inside 1.4 CAR points. (2) THE SWITCH ITSELF IS PRICED ON THIS BOOK FOR THE FIRST TIME - S-15 (b) measured it on the retired 3x champion at zero spread (22.383% / DD 31.4) and the current unlevered book had never been asked: removing it entirely earns 22.317% / Sharpe 1.026 / DD 36.892, i.e. +2.68 CAR points for +12.9 points of drawdown, paired +1.139 bps/day at t +0.96. That is REFUSED ON THE SPOT rather than filed in BLOCKERS.md as a risk-posture option, because 36.9% is past the 35% absolute limit in 'criteria' below - the one constraint here that is not a preference. The crisis switch is expensive and it is the only thing keeping this book inside its own risk mandate. NOTHING IS PROMOTABLE, NO NUMBER ABOVE MOVED: S1_REGIME_SERIES is unset in every deployed path and the switch reads the trailing realized volatility it has always read. The reusable rule is that a risk switch is not a forecasting problem - the shipped docstring and S-1 already record why (vol peaks coincide with the sharpest rebounds, so a realized switch is valuable BECAUSE IT IS LATE: it is a trailing stop denominated in volatility, acting on damage already done), and a forward-looking input converts it back into the anti-predictive 'risk-off above the median' filter the original S-1 write-up asked for and the data refused. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s29.py (--stage a / b / c).
stats_by_spread.delta_note: S-30 (2026-09-12): THE EQUITY ROUTE TO THE LEG SPLIT, PRICED AND REFUSED ON COST - AND THE 'DELTA BOOK' IT WAS BUILT ON DOES NOT EXIST. leg_note showed all of this book's measurable alpha is overnight; hedge_note removed the intraday leg with futures and was refused on DRAWDOWN at a breakeven 2.3x above its instrument's cost; risk_note re-measured it and was refused by 0.027 CAR points. S-30 asks the last question: shed the leg in the EQUITY book - sell a fraction h of the carried position at the open, hold none of it through the session, let the deployed close rebalance buy it back - and relever the freed variance. scripts/sweep_s30.py prices it on the same harness through a fourth default-inert argument (flat_frac on sweep_s25.legs_simulate, S-26/S-28's precedent); NO SHIPPED OR RUNNER-LOADED FILE WAS TOUCHED so no deploy gate is owed, and both identities are exact (flat_frac=0.0 gives 22.192150% / 5,052 orders, residual 5.33e-16; flat_frac=1.0 matches mode='overnight' on 3,689/3,689 sessions at max |difference| 0.000e+00). THE PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THAT SECOND IDENTITY: the delta routing saves 0.0x equity/yr, 0.0%, because a book holding NOTHING through the session has no delta at the open (the whole position must go) and none at the close (the reload IS the rebalance) - S-25's overnight book and S-30's are the same book to the cent. One correction survives: S-25's printed 1,248x was not growth-normalized and the same book normalized turns over 630.4x, exactly 2 x the 1.2496x gross. AT ZERO COST THE CONSTRUCTION WORKS AND CONFIRMS leg_note A THIRD TIME - Sharpe rises 1.159 -> 1.246 / 1.321 / 1.337 and drawdown falls 23.860 -> 21.467 / 19.051 / 19.113 at h = 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 - but the raw edge is NEGATIVE at every h (-0.749 to -3.050 bps/day, t -1.92 to -1.95), so the whole case is the relever, and THE PRE-REGISTERED BREAKEVEN REFUSES IT BEFORE ANY BOOK IS JUDGED: 1.948 / 1.730 / 1.474 / 1.145 bps ONE WAY at h = 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 1.00, under the 2 bp every other row in this file is charged, at every h, and HIGHEST WHERE THE CONSTRUCTION DOES LEAST - no interior optimum, which is the signature of a cost problem rather than a tuning one. Quoted as books at 2 bp + IBKR Pro financing (1.948 against 2.000 is 2.6% from the line, too narrow to leave as arithmetic): 14.689% / 0.937 / DD 21.909, 9.593 / 0.741 / 24.161, 4.497 / 0.427 / 29.405 and -0.555 / 0.009 / 50.206 against the deployed 19.640% / 1.047 / 24.037, PAIRED -1.875 / -3.819 / -5.792 / -7.785 BPS/DAY AT t -4.79 / -4.88 / -4.93 / -4.97 - the most significant refusal in this file, and the contrast with the zero-cost column (|t| <= 1.95) IS the spread. The exact vol-matched books are WORSE than the arithmetic that refused them, so the breakeven was a generous bound: h=0.50 at scale 1.381 earns 11.896% / 0.691 / DD 32.930 and h=1.00 at 1.646 earns -3.470% / -0.093 / DD 71.825, both BREACHING REG-T at 2.18x and 2.68x peak gross, failing both halves (IS 3.294 vs 14.317, OOS 17.589 vs 25.967 at h=0.50), because levering the book levers the spread bill linearly while the edge is sublinear once the larger financed debit is charged. The placebo passes: the mirror construction that sheds the leg that PAYS costs -15.395 bps/day at t -12.19 against -7.785 at t -4.97, twice as expensive on identical turnover. NOTHING IS PROMOTABLE AND NO NUMBER ABOVE MOVED: flat_frac is unset in every deployed path and this book holds around the clock as it always has. Nothing is filed in BLOCKERS.md either, because a refusal on cost is not an owner option. The reusable rule is that WHEN ONE CONSTRUCTION CAN BE EXPRESSED IN TWO INSTRUMENTS, THE REFUSAL MODE IDENTIFIES THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN THE IDEA: hedge_note's futures version cleared its instrument's cost by 2.3x and died on risk, this equity version dies on cost at 2.0x below its instrument's round trip, and the ratio between the two verdicts is just ES's 0.488 bps against an equity 4.0 bps round trip. The leg split is now confirmed by three independent routes and monetized by none. Reproduce with scripts/sweep_s30.py (--stage a, then --stage all --force-stage-b).
stats_by_spread.budget_note: S-31 (2026-09-12): THE SIZE DECISION IN 'BLOCKERS.md' WAS PRICED ON A BOOK THAT DOES NOT EXIST - ABOUT HALF THE ADVERTISED GAIN IS NOT THERE, AND THE SHARPE ARGUMENT FOR IT REVERSES. Every margin_budget table the owner has seen pays none of the three costs the notes above measure: S-16's frontier (0.75/0.78/0.80/0.82 -> 24.403 / 25.307 / 25.903 / 26.474) is LEAN at zero spread, zero financing, the backtest's clock, and S-21's (23.087 / 24.296 / 24.742) charges financing only. The correction CANNOT be a parallel shift, because the financing drag is proportional to the debit balance and the spread bill to turnover, and a larger budget raises both. scripts/sweep_s31.py runs eight budgets (0.70 to the Reg-T corner at 1.00) in four cost cells on the S-25/S-19 harness; the identity is exact (budget 0.75 gives 22.192150% / 5,052 orders at zero cost and 19.640168% / 1.047 / DD 24.037 fully charged, S-22's independent figure) and NO SHIPPED OR RUNNER-LOADED FILE WAS TOUCHED, so no deploy gate is owed.
